runs.text: The refinancing in March 2026 changed the shape of the debt. The company issued USD 700 million of 7.875% senior notes due 2034 and used the proceeds with cash to retire the notes due 2027 and part of the notes due 2028, so the next material maturities are the 2028 euro term loan and notes and the 2029 notes, together about USD 1,368 million, or about 35% of USD 3,872 million of debt principal [CP-1 debt table; Calculations]. This removes a near-term wall that the 10-K had flagged as unfunded absent refinancing, at the price of a higher stated coupon on the replacement paper than on the notes retired.

Leverage fell during 2026 but remains high, and management's own targets slipped. Management net leverage was about 4.9x at March 31, about 4.4x at June 30 and about 4.3x at September 30, 2026, driven by debt repaid from Kuan Yin land-sale proceeds rather than by earnings growth [CP-1 quarterly trajectory]. Over the same releases the full-year Adjusted EBITDA range was cut from USD 800 to 900 million to USD 775 to 800 million and the year-end leverage target moved from below 3.8x to below 4.2x. A creditor should treat the improvement as asset-sale deleveraging, which cannot repeat once the land is sold.

Earnings quality is weaker than the headline. Third-quarter 2026 net income of USD 196 million includes a USD 150 million insurance-related receipt booked against SG&A and a USD 50 million land gain, and full-year GAAP results include a USD 307 million nine-month tax provision after a full valuation allowance [CP-1 financials table]. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 200 million excludes these items, but it also excludes litigation and environmental charges that consume cash over 15 to 25 years. Segment mix has shifted: Titanium Technologies Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 85 million from USD 25 million on price, while Thermal and Specialized Solutions fell to USD 136 million from USD 194 million as the stationary aftermarket normalised after prior-year channel fill [CP-1 segment table].

Legacy obligations sit outside the leverage ratio and compete with debt service. Accrued litigation of USD 553 million and environmental remediation of USD 805 million at September 30, 2026 are not debt, yet the New Jersey order (USD 875 million over 25 years) and the North Carolina settlement (USD 455 million over 15 years, first payment of USD 51 million in October 2026) require annual cash [CP-1A transaction summary]. Part is funded by a USD 150 million insurance escrow and shared with DuPont and Corteva under the 2021 MOU, up to a cap. Including the reserves in debt on an illustrative basis raises leverage to about 6.1x (Calculations); that is a sensitivity, not a measure management or any covenant uses.

Liquidity is adequate on the balance-sheet date but its second leg is uncertain. Unrestricted cash of USD 698 million plus revolver availability of USD 953 million gave USD 1,651 million at September 30, 2026. A USD 220 million revolving tranche matured on October 7, 2026, and the filings do not say whether it was extended. If it was not, arithmetic availability would be USD 733 million. The revolver also carries a springing maturity linked to the 2028 and 2029 debt, so access to the revolver depends on that refinancing being completed in advance.

Cash generation covers interest but not by a wide margin. LTM free cash flow is about USD 211 million (Calculations) against USD 274 million of LTM net interest expense, with FCF flattered by the net USD 50 million of insurance escrow receipt over related settlement payments inside operating cash flow. Management's own full-year free cash flow guide is USD 120 to 160 million, and after dividends of roughly USD 50 million per year the margin for settlement payments and voluntary debt reduction is narrow.

Ratings and market signals confirm the pressure. Moody's downgraded to B1 from Ba3 on July 17, 2026 with a stable outlook; the only S&P statement in the sources is a stale April 16, 2025 affirmation of BB- with negative outlook. The sources contain no market quotes or spreads, so no market-implied view is offered.

runs.text: Strengths. Liquidity is solid at the reporting date: USD 698 million of unrestricted cash, no revolver borrowings and USD 953 million of availability, with management stating that sources are sufficient through at least the end of November 2027 [Management Language, CP-1 liquidity bridge]. The maturity profile has been extended: the senior secured term loan in dollars is due in October 2032 and no bond matures before November 2028 [Documentary Fact]. Customer concentration is low, with no customer above 10% of net sales and about 2,400 customers across about 110 countries [Documentary Fact, CP-1A]. Demand drivers are partly regulatory (AIM Act and F-Gas transitions to Opteon) and partly price-led recovery in TiO2, with growth in Performance Solutions serving data center and semiconductor markets [Documentary Fact for the regulation, Management Language for growth claims]. The company has acted creditor-supportively on capital allocation, cutting the dividend and repaying debt from asset sales [Documentary Fact, CP-1A].

Weaknesses. Leverage is high on any basis shown and the improvement came from asset-sale proceeds [Analyst Interpretation, CP-1 bridges]. Legacy PFAS and environmental liabilities are large, multi-decade and uncertain in scale, and only part is cost-shared [Documentary Fact]. Earnings are concentrated in a cyclical product (TiO2) and a regulation-timed product (Opteon aftermarket) whose year-over-year trend turned negative in the third quarter [Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation]. Reported GAAP results are volatile because of litigation, valuation allowance and gain items, which complicates covenant and add-back reading [Documentary Fact]. The financing documents are not in the pack, so guarantor coverage, restricted-payment capacity and covenant headroom cannot be verified [Insufficient Information]. A history of restated prior periods and a past Audit Committee review raise the weight a creditor should place on reconciling adjusted measures to filings [Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The supplied sources contain no sponsor transaction, merger or leveraged recapitalisation, and the context lists no deal terms. The transactions that matter to a creditor are a refinancing, debt paydown from asset-sale proceeds, a land sale, and legal settlements. This is a documentary summary. Figures reproduce CP-1 or cite a locator.

On March 12, 2026 the company closed a private offering of 7.875% senior notes due 2034 in an aggregate principal amount of 700, issued under the 2020 base indenture as supplemented by a Fourth Supplemental Indenture, with a guarantor named in the agreement but not named in the supplied text (Q3 10-Q page:27). Use of proceeds: together with cash on hand, the redemption of 188 of the 5.750% senior notes due 2028 and the redemption of all 495 of the 5.375% senior notes due 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:27). This addressed the nearest unsecured maturity: the 10-K had warned that "the Company would not have sufficient funds to repay this indebtedness at maturity absent refinancing or other capital-raising actions" (10-K page:170). The refinancing extended the unsecured maturity profile at a higher stated coupon than the notes it replaced. The coupon comparison is a documentary comparison of two stated rates and not a cost-of-debt analysis.

The company also repaid part of the euro term loan due August 2028 using land-sale proceeds and cash: EUR 140 million in April 2026 per the Q1 release, EUR 230 million in the second quarter per the Q2 release, and EUR 280 million in the nine months per the Q3 10-Q (Q1 ER page:4; Q2 ER page:5; Q3 10-Q page:26). The release amounts and the filing amount are labelled differently (April payment, quarter payment and nine-month total) and are logged here without reconciliation. A loss on extinguishment of debt is reported for the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:26). The debt balances after these actions are in the CP-1 handoff.

The Kuan Yin, Taiwan property: the company closed the site in 2023 as part of the Titanium Technologies Transformation Plan (Q3 10-Q page:16). In April 2026 it sold nine of ten land parcels for net proceeds of about 287 (Q1 ER page:4), and the Q3 release says the sale of the property was completed for total net consideration of about 340 including the remaining parcel for 56 of gross proceeds (Q3 ER page:1). A gain on sale of 316 for nine months 2026 is in the CP-1 handoff. About 25 of tax related to the sale was paid in Q3 (Q3 ER page:5). The proceeds are the stated source of debt reduction (Q1 ER page:1). Management Language: "positioning the Company to paydown" debt. This is a one-time source of liquidity and not recurring cash flow.

Legal settlements with cash consequences: a New Jersey judicial consent order was finalized in September 2026 with scheduled payments totalling 875 over 25 years, a first payment of 100 in September 2026, and a related PFAS Insurance MOU under which Corteva and DuPont funded 150 into an escrow for the company's New Jersey payments (Q3 10-Q page:155, page:39). A North Carolina settlement was entered in September 2026 with total payments of 455 over 15 years and a first payment of 51 in October 2026, which is a subsequent event relative to September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:116). A June 2026 consent decree with the EPA and the West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection carries a 23 civil penalty and a commitment to fund 90 of projects over 15 years (Q3 10-Q page:111). These are cash obligations that compete with debt service. Management's net leverage measure does not include them (CP-1 handoff, obligations outside management net debt).

Other 2026 events: a 2026 Restructuring Program with employee separation charges was begun in the first quarter (Q3 10-Q page:14); the exit from the SPS Capstone business was completed in 2025 (Q2 ER page:2); an operational outage at the Washington Works site reduced APM volumes in the first half and was reported resolved by the second quarter (Q1 ER page:2; Q2 ER page:3); the company launched a liquid cooling portfolio under the Faizeon brand (Q3 ER page:1).

New debt issues and amendments: 7.875% senior notes due 2034, 700, closed March 12, 2026. Credit Agreement Amendment No. 4 in October 2025 extended the U.S. dollar term loan from August 2028 to October 2032 with a wider margin (Q3 10-Q page:26). Moody's downgrade followed on July 17, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:149). Documents for the notes and the amendments are not supplied, so covenant and guarantee terms remain unverified. Draft or unexecuted status: none of the described transactions is described as draft; the North Carolina settlement is described as entered into and its first payment as made after the quarter. A settlement in principle with about 2,900 private well owners is described as not final (Q3 10-Q page:116).

fields.value: - Revolver maturity timing: the Q3 10-Q states the "$220 in revolving commitments that matured on October 7, 2026" (page:25) and still lists "$953 million" revolver availability "as of September 30, 2026" (page:149). The commitment matured after the balance-sheet date and before the as-of date. This is a subsequent event relative to September 30, 2026. The filings do not say whether the $220 million tranche was extended or replaced. Availability after October 7, 2026 is therefore not established. Downstream use must keep the balance-sheet-date figure and the post-balance-sheet maturity apart. Severity high for CP-1 and CP-2.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Evidence: the Q3 10-Q debt note and liquidity discussion give facility-level balances, covenant-compliance language and a revolver whose $220 million tranche "matured on October 7, 2026". Source risk mechanism: filing notes summarise rather than reproduce the executed agreements, and the filing's own balance-sheet-date availability may overstate availability on the as-of date. Downstream consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 can describe and measure the capital structure from the filings but must state that revolver availability after October 7, 2026, covenant headroom and guarantor identity are not established. The next evidence action is to obtain the Credit Agreement with Amendments No. 1 to No. 4 and the indentures, and to look for any filing after September 30, 2026 that addresses the matured revolver tranche.

Dividends declared fell from 1.00 per share in FY2024 to 0.5125 in FY2025 and to a quarterly 0.0875 in 2026 (10-K page:162; Q3 10-Q page:156), and the company used land-sale proceeds and cash to repay debt (Q1 ER page:1; Q3 10-Q page:26). These are deleveraging actions that support creditors. Capital returned in the nine months of 2026 was 39 in dividends and none in buybacks (CP-1 handoff). Behaviour category: Supportive or Neutral on the documented actions, with the caveat that willingness is separate from legal capacity and feasibility. Legal capacity to pay dividends, make restricted payments or incur debt depends on the Credit Agreement and indenture baskets, which are not supplied (Insufficient Information). Feasibility is constrained by the leverage and liquidity facts in CP-1.

The 10-K lists regulatory inquiries and litigation that may arise from that review as a risk (10-K page:4). The supplied text does not say that a material weakness was identified; this is not established either way beyond the risk-factor language, so it is Insufficient Information. Mechanism: reliability of reported adjusted measures and add-backs matters because leverage covenants and management leverage ratios depend on them.

Mechanism: cash settlements are paid over 15 to 25 years and are not classified as debt, which can reduce cash available for debt service and for refinancing without changing reported leverage. Implication for monitoring: track annual settlement payments against free cash flow.

fields.value: 1. Revenue durability: evidence is the mix of regulation-driven Opteon demand, TiO2 pricing actions and growth in Performance Solutions (10-K page:12; Q3 ER page:3 to page:4). fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Chemours is a stretched but liquid credit: near-term debt service looks manageable, while leverage and legacy obligations are the weak points. Its strongest support is USD 698 million of unrestricted cash, no revolver borrowings, no bond or term loan maturity of size before 2028 and a TiO2 price recovery that lifted third-quarter 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to USD 200 million. Its weakest point is management net leverage of about 4.3x, which leaves out USD 1,358 million of litigation and environmental reserves, with LTM interest cover of about 2.7x. The outcome turns on whether TiO2 pricing holds, whether the cooling aftermarket stabilises, and how the 2028 and 2029 refinancing meets settlement payments. Confidence is Medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Confidence is below High because CP-1A and CP-0 record that executed financing documents are not supplied, that revolver capacity after the October 7, 2026 maturity of the 220 tranche is not stated, and that interim cash interest and tax are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The refinancing in March 2026 changed the shape of the debt. The company issued USD 700 million of 7.875% senior notes due 2034 and used the proceeds with cash to retire the notes due 2027 and part of the notes due 2028, so the next material maturities are the 2028 euro term loan and notes and the 2029 notes, together about USD 1,368 million, or about 35% of USD 3,872 million of debt principal [CP-1 debt table; Calculations]. This removes a near-term wall that the 10-K had flagged as unfunded absent refinancing, at the price of a higher stated coupon on the replacement paper than on the notes retired.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage fell during 2026 but remains high, and management's own targets slipped. Management net leverage was about 4.9x at March 31, about 4.4x at June 30 and about 4.3x at September 30, 2026, driven by debt repaid from Kuan Yin land-sale proceeds rather than by earnings growth [CP-1 quarterly trajectory]. Over the same releases the full-year Adjusted EBITDA range was cut from USD 800 to 900 million to USD 775 to 800 million and the year-end leverage target moved from below 3.8x to below 4.2x. A creditor should treat the improvement as asset-sale deleveraging, which cannot repeat once the land is sold.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality is weaker than the headline. Third-quarter 2026 net income of USD 196 million includes a USD 150 million insurance-related receipt booked against SG&A and a USD 50 million land gain, and full-year GAAP results include a USD 307 million nine-month tax provision after a full valuation allowance [CP-1 financials table]. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 200 million excludes these items, but it also excludes litigation and environmental charges that consume cash over 15 to 25 years. Segment mix has shifted: Titanium Technologies Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 85 million from USD 25 million on price, while Thermal and Specialized Solutions fell to USD 136 million from USD 194 million as the stationary aftermarket normalised after prior-year channel fill [CP-1 segment table].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Legacy obligations sit outside the leverage ratio and compete with debt service. Accrued litigation of USD 553 million and environmental remediation of USD 805 million at September 30, 2026 are not debt, yet the New Jersey order (USD 875 million over 25 years) and the North Carolina settlement (USD 455 million over 15 years, first payment of USD 51 million in October 2026) require annual cash [CP-1A transaction summary]. Part is funded by a USD 150 million insurance escrow and shared with DuPont and Corteva under the 2021 MOU, up to a cap. Including the reserves in debt on an illustrative basis raises leverage to about 6.1x (Calculations); that is a sensitivity, not a measure management or any covenant uses.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate on the balance-sheet date but its second leg is uncertain. Unrestricted cash of USD 698 million plus revolver availability of USD 953 million gave USD 1,651 million at September 30, 2026. A USD 220 million revolving tranche matured on October 7, 2026, and the filings do not say whether it was extended. If it was not, arithmetic availability would be USD 733 million. The revolver also carries a springing maturity linked to the 2028 and 2029 debt, so access to the revolver depends on that refinancing being completed in advance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation covers interest but not by a wide margin. LTM free cash flow is about USD 211 million (Calculations) against USD 274 million of LTM net interest expense, with FCF flattered by the net USD 50 million of insurance escrow receipt over related settlement payments inside operating cash flow. Management's own full-year free cash flow guide is USD 120 to 160 million, and after dividends of roughly USD 50 million per year the margin for settlement payments and voluntary debt reduction is narrow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ratings and market signals confirm the pressure. Moody's downgraded to B1 from Ba3 on July 17, 2026 with a stable outlook; the only S&P statement in the sources is a stale April 16, 2025 affirmation of BB- with negative outlook. The sources contain no market quotes or spreads, so no market-implied view is offered.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Liquidity is solid at the reporting date: USD 698 million of unrestricted cash, no revolver borrowings and USD 953 million of availability, with management stating that sources are sufficient through at least the end of November 2027 [Management Language, CP-1 liquidity bridge]. The maturity profile has been extended: the senior secured term loan in dollars is due in October 2032 and no bond matures before November 2028 [Documentary Fact]. Customer concentration is low, with no customer above 10% of net sales and about 2,400 customers across about 110 countries [Documentary Fact, CP-1A]. Demand drivers are partly regulatory (AIM Act and F-Gas transitions to Opteon) and partly price-led recovery in TiO2, with growth in Performance Solutions serving data center and semiconductor markets [Documentary Fact for the regulation, Management Language for growth claims]. The company has acted creditor-supportively on capital allocation, cutting the dividend and repaying debt from asset sales [Documentary Fact, CP-1A].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Leverage is high on any basis shown and the improvement came from asset-sale proceeds [Analyst Interpretation, CP-1 bridges]. Legacy PFAS and environmental liabilities are large, multi-decade and uncertain in scale, and only part is cost-shared [Documentary Fact]. Earnings are concentrated in a cyclical product (TiO2) and a regulation-timed product (Opteon aftermarket) whose year-over-year trend turned negative in the third quarter [Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation]. Reported GAAP results are volatile because of litigation, valuation allowance and gain items, which complicates covenant and add-back reading [Documentary Fact]. The financing documents are not in the pack, so guarantor coverage, restricted-payment capacity and covenant headroom cannot be verified [Insufficient Information]. A history of restated prior periods and a past Audit Committee review raise the weight a creditor should place on reconciling adjusted measures to filings [Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation].
